ch05.heading: Chapter 5: Riffle’s River
recap: On Moonpaw’s fourth morning, the old tom was guarding the pile with his eyes shut and a snail on his ear, and four more pieces were gone: sixteen in four nights.
Tallyheart taught Moonpaw her fifth Count, nine lives: a ten with one claw tucked in.
Moonpaw sat through the Roar, the apprentices’ courage test, on the otters’ raft, and did not move one of nine claws. Tallyheart counted.
Under the raft she found Puddle, who has four big feet and says he is a log. Puddle saw clever little paws picking up mice on the storm night.
The old ferry otter said the fox had told him the dragon story, twice, and showed Moonpaw a tuft of thin brown fur.
Patience the heron said there was no moon on the storm night, and that two small shapes crossed her mud. There were tiny prints in it. It cost eighteen fish.
Moonpaw sat still until a pale reed blinked. It was Wisp, who stands on one leg like a heron, and drew a fox dropping something glittering in the reeds.
Under the Old Bridge, Sprinkle lit a forepaw for everyone found so far. Mama’s count is coming back.
That night, Tallyheart said every warrior has sat through the Roar. She counted through hers, very loudly.

puddle.name: Puddle
lines: Blue-grey, with feet much too big for him. He says he is a log.
Moonpaw found him under the otters’ ferry raft. Mama says: stay where you land.
He says five, and then he sinks. He always pops up again. Five more claws, counted.

recap: On Moonpaw’s fourth morning, the old tom was guarding the pile with his eyes shut and a snail on his ear, and four more pieces were gone: sixteen in four nights.
Tallyheart taught Moonpaw her fifth Count, nine lives: a ten with one claw tucked in.
Moonpaw sat through the Roar, the apprentices’ courage test, on the otters’ raft, and did not move one of nine claws. Tallyheart counted.
The old ferry otter said the fox had told him the dragon story, twice, and showed Moonpaw a tuft of thin brown fur.
Patience the heron said there was no moon on the storm night, and that two small shapes crossed her mud. There were tiny prints in it. It cost eighteen fish.
That night, Tallyheart said every warrior has sat through the Roar. She counted through hers, very loudly.

ch05.heading: Chapter 5: Riffle’s River
recap: On Moonpaw’s fourth morning, the old tom was guarding the pile with his eyes shut and a snail on his ear, and four more pieces were gone: sixteen in four nights.
Tallyheart taught Moonpaw her fifth Count, nine lives: a ten with one claw tucked in.
Moonpaw sat through the Roar, the apprentices’ courage test, on the otters’ raft, and did not move one of nine claws. Tallyheart counted.
The old ferry otter said the fox had told him the dragon story, twice, and showed Moonpaw a tuft of thin brown fur.
Patience the heron said there was no moon on the storm night, and that two small shapes crossed her mud. There were tiny prints in it. It cost eighteen fish.
That night, Tallyheart said every warrior has sat through the Roar. She counted through hers, very loudly.

ch05.heading: Chapter 5: Riffle’s River
recap: On Moonpaw’s fourth morning, the old tom was guarding the pile with his eyes shut and a snail on his ear, and four more pieces were gone: sixteen in four nights.
Tallyheart taught Moonpaw her fifth Count, nine lives: a ten with one claw tucked in.
On the roof of her old tower, she found Squall, the littlest dragonet, who told her about two skinny shapes that go to the tracks every night.
Moonpaw sat through the Roar, the apprentices’ courage test, on the otters’ raft, and did not move one of nine claws. Tallyheart counted.
Under the raft she found Puddle, who has four big feet and says he is a log. Puddle saw clever little paws picking up mice on the storm night.
The old ferry otter said the fox had told him the dragon story, twice, and showed Moonpaw a tuft of thin brown fur.
Patience the heron said there was no moon on the storm night, and that two small shapes crossed her mud. There were tiny prints in it. It cost eighteen fish.
Under the Old Bridge, Sprinkle lit a forepaw for everyone found so far. Mama’s count is coming back.
That night, Tallyheart said every warrior has sat through the Roar. She counted through hers, very loudly.

puddle.name: Puddle
lines: Blue-grey, with feet much too big for him. He says he is a log.
Moonpaw found him under the otters’ ferry raft. Mama says: stay where you land.
He says five, and then he sinks. He always pops up again. Five more claws, counted.
